game_title: The Lost Legacy of C · History/classification review
game_concept: A tower defense set in Sand Dunes – Buried Temple Steps, steps of a half-buried temple: the camel trader must handle sandstorms while practicing debugging & combined skills. Core idea – Syntax Sweep: Spot and fix syntax errors such as missing colons or brackets before the program runs.
theme: Sand Dunes – Buried Temple Steps: steps of a half-buried temple
core_gameplay_loop: Search the archive, examine recovered computing artifacts, and use their evidence to verify the assigned C lesson.
player_objective: Case 6: Find 5 artifacts, read the evidence, and verify three findings about History/classification review.
controls: Select objects in the room. Review discovered objects in Evidence and verify your findings. Tab and Enter select controls. Escape closes a card or pauses.
win_condition: Recover all 5 artifacts and answer all three evidence checks correctly.
lose_condition: The case ends when the available incorrect evidence checks are exhausted.
assets_style: Shared archive artwork, illustrated artifacts, and Kenney interface audio.
duplicate_check_notes: Unique combination of primary mechanic 'Syntax Sweep' (Week 9 slot 1), mission type 'Survival Siege', and setting 'Buried Temple Steps'. No other file shares this combination; games sharing the mechanic differ in mission/win condition and setting, and games sharing the setting use a different mechanic.
topic: Introduction to C: History, Characteristics and Classification

region.name: Sand Dunes

tutorial: Match the silhouettes in the tray to the objects in the room.

source_player_objective: Protect the camel pen from sandstorms in Buried Temple Steps: keep the syntax_errors meter above zero by applying the concept correctly until the 36-second timer ends.
source_lose_condition: syntax_errors drops to 0, or lives reach 0, before the 36-second timer ends.
source_game_title: Syntax Sweep – Buried Temple Steps Defense
hint: Match an unfound object in the tray to its shape in the room. The Evidence folder keeps every record you uncover.
